title: Searching for the ox
hook: picture one: the herder searches, not knowing what he's lost (Ox-Herding 1)
tomorrow: why would a Zen picture send the herder to the books?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ten pictures: a Zen teacher's series of a herder and his ox, start to finish. Today the first one opens.

Open the fridge, stand there, forget what you came for: Kuoan's first picture is that moment, stretched across a whole landscape. A herder stands alone in tall grass, pushing it aside with both hands. In the verse Kuoan, a Chinese Zen teacher, wrote beside it, the rivers are wide, the mountains far, and the path keeps going. He's worn out. Evening comes, and all he hears is cicadas in the maple trees. He's looking for his ox, and he couldn't tell you where he lost it.
screen: `WHAT DID I COME FOR?` → `ALONE IN TALL GRASS.` → `ONLY CICADAS AT EVENING.`

segments.voice: Here's the strange part. The short preface to this picture says the ox was never lost. So why search? Because, it says, the herder turned his back on himself, and the ox wandered off into the dust. Home looks farther away every day. He stands at crossroads, unsure which way to go, burning with wanting to gain and fearing to lose. Notice what's missing from that list: a map. He isn't searching because he's clever. He's searching because something in him won't settle. That's the teaching, and it's Zen's own: what you're looking for is your own true nature, what Zen teachers call Buddha-nature, and it was never somewhere else. The search doesn't make it. The search begins because you looked away. And Kuoan doesn't mock the herder. He makes the searching itself the first picture of the way, drawn with the same care as the last. Tired, a little lost, hearing cicadas: that's where the path starts, even while the searcher thinks he's nowhere. This path started the same way, with one breath at the bottom of a hill and no idea what the climb was for. One to tell a friend tonight: the ox in these pictures isn't a prize you win. It stands for the very self that's doing the looking.
screen: `THE OX WAS NEVER LOST.` · `HE TURNED HIS BACK ON HIMSELF.` · `YOUR OWN TRUE NATURE.` · `SEARCHING IS PICTURE ONE.` · then, large: `SEARCHING.`

segments.voice: Find any scrap of paper and write one line by hand: why you began this, back at the bottom of the hill, in whatever words come. Then sit with it for the two minutes, the way the herder stands in the grass, not knowing yet.
Searching for the ox: Kuoan's first picture, a herder alone in the grass, looking for what was never lost.
Keep this one: searching, the picture Kuoan drew first, before any ox appears. Day three of the summit, done.
